children: The U.S. dollar's bias against its Singapore counterpart remains upward, based on the daily and weekly charts, says Quek Ser Leang of UOB Global Economics & Markets Research in a note. The U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair's weekly moving average convergence divergence indicator seems poised to cross into positive territory, the senior technical strategist notes. Also, the currency pair has risen clearly above the upper boundary of the daily Ichimoku cloud, but the top of weekly cloud capped its gains at 1.2871 this week, the strategist says. Hence, the currency pair must break above 1.2871 to extend its advance, the strategist adds. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% higher at 1.2825 Singapore dollars, FactSet data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
